chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Pre-emption is not for the Jew and the Christian.
And he said: There is no pre-emption except for a partner who has not been distributed (his share).
And he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The trustee of the orphan is at the status of his father. He takes the pre-emption for him if it was an advantage for him in it.
And he said: For the absentee is pre-emption.

key_terms.شُفْعَةٌ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal to buy a co-owned property)

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in Islamic law according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the scope of 'shuf'ah' (pre-emption) by excluding Ahl al-Kitab while affirming it for partners, orphans' trustees, and absent owners. It reflects the Shia juristic view that pre-emption is a right tied to specific relational or ownership ties rather than general proximity, emphasizing the trustee's role as a legal extension of the father. The narration underscores the practical application of property rights in maintaining communal harmony and protecting vulnerable parties' interests.
